# 0028. Show the props evidence makes relevant, and schedule the checker by what will be shown

**Status:** Proposed **Date:** 2026-11-15

## Context

Every surface returns every prop the checker resolves, minus what a collapsed layer hides. That is useless to Storybook and to agents: Chakra's `Button` had about 1,141 argTypes before the collapse-by-relevance PR (`feat/collapse-large-sources-by-default`) and 146 after it, and the rows still hidden are the ones consumers pass. Measured on origin/main 7b8f6d0d with the checker (trail 405 T5, `caliper-fixtures/shrink/relevance-baseline.md`), the share of the props a component's call sites pass that the output lists is 0.43 on shadcn (mean over 408 components; median 0.50), 0.86 on Mantine, 0.91 on ant-design and 0.96 on react-spectrum. Nearly every miss is a DOM attribute in a collapsed `React.ComponentProps<"el">` layer (shadcn: `className` alone on 243 components), and those layers carry `htmlElement` with no `members` and `totalProps` 0, so a reader cannot tell what is inside them. Today's choices come from size and from name lists (`resolver/ambient.rs`'s `*StyleProps`, `GlobalDOMEvents` clauses; `notable_html_attrs` in `react_types.rs:462`), which the owner rules out.

The checker's cost follows what it converts, not what is shown. A whole-project `extract` of Chakra's own repository built 42 GB of `PropType` trees converting its style system (`shrink/chakra-memory.md`), and the only memory guard (`OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`, `crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs:93`) reads the checker's arenas (`crates/semantic/src/checker.rs:169`), not the converter's heap, and only between requests (`on_demand.rs:643`).

## Decision

### A. Relevance decides what is shown, from evidence

The owner's rules: returning all resolved props is useless for Storybook and agents; relevance decides what to show; it is derived from evidence, with no name lists; agent output is narrowed later.

**Signals.** Each prop a component's props type reaches gets evidence from four places.

- **The props type.** A member the props type declares itself is always shown. So is each key of `Pick<X, 'a' | 'b'>`, named on purpose; `Omit<X, 'k'>` says only that `k` is gone, nothing about the rest. A member that redeclares or narrows a base member is the component's own. A required member is shown (a story cannot render without it), and so is one with a `@default` tag or a destructuring default in the body (the component handles it). JSDoc and a literal-union type do not show a member on their own: as promoters they would list every documented member of a style system; they order the shown rows (open question 1).
- **Spreads in the body** (T1's `ComponentMapping::body`). `{...rest}` on a DOM tag passes the ambient DOM attributes: no evidence, ignored. A spread onto a component is one hop to that component's own non-ambient props, with the JSX tag resolved to the component by symbol and import (ADR 0027's identity, never the display name). An attribute set after the spread is fixed and subtracted; one set before it is an overridable default and kept; an attribute whose value is one of the component's own props adds nothing. A name in `reads` is shown when its source is not ambient.
- **Call sites.** The props consumers pass at JSX usages across the project (T1's `SourceData::jsx_usages`) and in stories' `args`, counted per component with a floor of `max(2, 20%)` of its sites. The baseline puts the cost at 0.30 (Mantine), 0.03 (Spectrum), 0.76 (shadcn) and 0.24 (antd) extra entries per component.
- **Unknown.** When `handed_on` is true, `reads` is incomplete (T1's contract), and the body says nothing: never guessed. The member falls back to today's single collapse decision with the reaching count (`CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` in the collapse PR; on main it is still `ResolutionContext::collapses`, `resolver/mod.rs:595`, by declared count, so `decide` is wired only after that PR merges), so missing evidence never hides more than today.

**Ambient** is decided by where a member is declared, not by its name: a member `@types/react` declares (by declaring path, as `is_react_declared` in `crates/semantic/src/component.rs` recognizes React terminals), or one that reaches the component only through a spread onto a DOM tag. Each lane computes the bit for each prop and hands it to `decide` in `Evidence` (`is_react_declared` is private to `caliper-docgen-semantic`, which core does not depend on); `decide` never recomputes it, and a model test in the style of the collapse PR's `collapse_model.rs` holds the two lanes to the same bits. `ambient.rs`'s name clauses and `notable_html_attrs` stay as the unknown-evidence fallback until the T5 gate shows evidence replaces them; then they are deleted (slice R9).

**Combination.** One function, `relevance::decide(&Evidence) -> Shown`, owns it, as `CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` owns collapsing; both lanes and every surface call it.

- Shown as a row: own, picked, overriding, required, defaulted; a non-ambient member that is forwarded, read, or passed at the floor.
- Named in the layer's `used` list: an ambient member passed at the floor or read in the body.
- Left in a collapsed layer: everything else with complete evidence, even from a source today's rule lists (its source becomes a layer). A non-ambient member with unknown body evidence and no other signal is listed or collapsed as today.

**Output.** A collapsed `InheritedLayer` (`crates/core/src/types/output.rs:83`) gains `used`: the names of its members that evidence put forward, written once as a name list (ADR 0018), not as typed rows. Universal props such as `className`, `style` and `id` cost a name each instead of a row each. A `React.ComponentProps<"el">` layer also gets its `members`, so a reader can check `used` against it. No per-prop flag in this ADR: the row/layer split already says shown or not, and why a row is shown is for the agent output, deferred. `SCHEMA_VERSION` goes from 7 to 8 (ADR 0017), with the RDT view, the JSON schema, `binding.d.ts` and a changeset.

**Consumers.** The Storybook addon makes argTypes from rows, then one name-only row per `used` name with the layer as its category; an option (`relevance: 'all'`) asks for the expanded output, which is today's `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'`. CLI JSON and TOON carry the same output. Agent output keeps its current form until the agent flow is narrowed.

**Acceptance gate** (T5's metric, ported into the weekly by T4). Coverage counts a passed prop as visible when it is a row or in `used`. Call-site evidence is computed from half of the files (by path hash) and coverage is measured on the other half, so the gate does not pass by construction. On the half the floor is `max(1, 20%)`, and only components with at least 6 sites are measured, so the gate does not test a stricter rule than the one shipped.

- Coverage mean rises: shadcn 0.43 to at least 0.70; Mantine 0.86 to at least 0.88; antd 0.91 to at least 0.93; Spectrum stays at least 0.96.
- Rows shown fall: the median rows per component does not rise on any corpus (Mantine 77, Spectrum 74, shadcn 3, antd 17), and total rows fall on Mantine and Spectrum. Chakra `Button`'s typed rows stay at or under 146 (its `used` names come on top and are reported apart).
- These targets are proposals. Only the extra-entry costs above were measured; the fall in rows is not predicted.

### B. The checker is scheduled by the props that will be shown

The owner asked for a queue. Its parts, against what exists:

- **Item.** The props of one component that relevance will show, at one revision, not the whole component; collapsed members are listed by name and parent and never converted. Exists: `SemanticTarget::react_wanted` and `described` (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs:169-175`) already narrow what one target converts. New: a `shown` set from `relevance::decide`.
- **Priority classes**, on-screen > neighbouring stories > background fill. Exists: two (`Priority::Interactive` and `Background`, `types/semantic.rs:221`), two lanes with a starvation bound and raising (`Queue`, `on_demand.rs:150-199`, `INTERACTIVE_STREAK` 4), a raise when an on-screen request joins a queued one (`pipeline/semantic_hook.rs:256`). The addon's prefetch queue holds the next `prefetchStories - 1` stories, replaced on every selection (`packages/storybook/src/background.ts:39`, `preset.ts:150`, `prefetch.ts:32`), one story at a time (`background.ts:81-89`), and asks at `Background` (`pipeline/watch.rs:464`). New: a third class, `Neighbour`, between them.
- **Preemption and cancel.** Exists: an edit forgets every kept and pending answer in the hook (`semantic_hook.rs:180`); the lifecycle reducer refreshes an answer superseded by an edit (`lifecycle.ts:196`); navigation replaces the addon's queue. Missing: nothing reaches `OnDemand`'s queue, which has no cancel, so requests nobody waits for still run. New: a request carries a cancel token tripped by an edit or by the navigation that replaced it, dropped when taken. Raising a request clears its token: an on-screen request that joined a queued prefetch (`Found::Joined`, `semantic_hook.rs:256`) is waited for, so a navigation never cancels it; and preemption between components of one request (a tsrs call cannot be interrupted).
- **Batching by snapshot.** Exists: `OnDemand` keeps one snapshot and re-roots it per request (`Checker::snapshot_for`, `on_demand.rs:551`); the one-shot CLI answers every component on one program with eight files in flight sharing one converter (`crates/semantic/src/lib.rs:49`, `session`). A request whose roots differ re-roots the snapshot (`rerooted`, `on_demand.rs:574`), which makes a new one with new type ids. New: the worker takes the queued items of one class together and roots one snapshot at the union of their roots, so they share the program and one converter memo; the memo is dropped with that snapshot, never carried to an updated or re-rooted one (type ids are valid within one snapshot, ADR 0026). The memo is per request today.
- **Admission on a memory budget.** Exists: the arena guard (`Upkeep::decide`, `on_demand.rs:709`), which misses the converter heap. In flight: the one-shot heap budget (heap-budget slice B, branch `feat/one-shot-heap-budget`, no commits yet), counting converted nodes inside conversion. New: the scheduler admits a background item only under a soft budget read from the allocator, holds background work above it, and stops the checker above the hard one, as `stop_past_bound` does.
- **Stream each result.** Exists: one `Delivery` per request (`types/semantic.rs:256`), and the reducer turns each settled key into a refresh (`lifecycle.ts:185-205`, invariants 1 to 6). New: a request of several keys delivers each key when converted. The CLI keeps one write: canonical JSON interns props across components (ADR 0009, 0018).

Not determined: whether tsrs's memory allows the converter memo to live as long as a snapshot over a long session (ADR 0026 measured 98 to 246 MB over 150 edits without it); whether `mi_process_info` reads the same under the napi host; how far listing collapsed members without converting them lowers the 42 GB case, since the collapse PR collapses `SystemProperties` after conversion.

## Consequences

- Output changes on every surface; the addon's default argTypes change again after the collapse PR. Complete evidence hides on purpose props today lists (a 10-prop dependency source the body never reads becomes a layer); that is how rows fall. Only a prop with unknown evidence is guaranteed to be shown as today.
- Agents read the same narrowed output until their flow is designed.
- Call-site evidence makes a component's answer depend on other files. Watch and the kept answer must invalidate on a consumer's edit, and the per-component closure is still unknown (ADR 0026), so invalidation stays whole-project.
- The scheduler adds a third class, cancel tokens and a long-lived memo to `OnDemand`; its determinism gate (gate harness) must hold with cancels.
- Breaking for readers of `InheritedLayer` (schema 8).

## Alternatives considered

- **A fixed universal set** (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `ref` plus handlers): about the same 1 to 3 rows, but a name list.
- **Expand everything** (`none`): 280 to 1,100 rows per component (`--no-checker` figures in the baseline).
- **Whole components as queue items**: converts collapsed members nobody sees, which is where the Chakra memory went.

## Slice plan

Files are disjoint within a wave; a file two slices touch is named with the order. Each slice runs `just lint doc-check machete typos`; a test that fails on main first.

**Wave 0, now:** R0.

- **R0, the decision function.** Owns `crates/core/src/relevance/mod.rs` (new), one line in `crates/core/src/lib.rs`. `Evidence`, `Shown`, `decide`, a table test per rule above. It also creates every wave-1 module empty and declares it (`relevance/props_type.rs`, `forwarding.rs`, `call_sites.rs`, `extractor/story_args.rs`, `extractor/factory_props.rs`, with their `mod` lines in `relevance/mod.rs` and `extractor/mod.rs`), so no wave-1 slice edits a shared `mod.rs`. About 200 lines. Depends on nothing. First failing test: `an_inherited_member_the_body_never_reads_stays_in_its_layer`. Gate: core nextest.

**Wave 1, after R0, the collapse PR and PR 470 (T1) merge; up to three at once, in this order of value:**

- **T3, forwarding.** Owns `relevance/forwarding.rs` (new), `crates/core/tests/relevance_forwarding.rs`. Resolves a spread's tag by symbol and import, takes one hop of own non-ambient props, subtracts attributes after the spread. About 400 lines. Depends on R0 and PR 470. First failing test: `a_rest_spread_onto_a_component_shows_its_own_props_except_those_set_after_it`. Gate: core nextest.
- **T6, call sites.** Owns `relevance/call_sites.rs`, `crates/core/src/extractor/story_args.rs` (new). Counts `jsx_usages` and stories' `args` per component at the floor. About 350 lines. Depends on R0 and PR 470. First failing test: `a_prop_passed_at_a_quarter_of_the_sites_is_used_and_one_at_a_tenth_is_not`. Gate: core nextest.
- **T2, props-type signals.** Owns `relevance/props_type.rs` (new), `crates/core/tests/relevance_props_type.rs`. Own, picked, overriding (the checker's `declarations`, ADR 0026 S7a), required, defaulted. About 300 lines. Depends on R0 and the collapse PR. First failing test: `a_member_that_narrows_a_base_member_is_a_row_when_its_source_collapses`. Gate: core nextest, `just test-checker-lane`.
- **F1, factory own props.** Owns `crates/core/src/extractor/factory_props.rs` (new), the field in `types/collected.rs` (after PR 470, which also edits it). `chakra("div", {variants})` gives its variant keys; Spectrum's `createLeafComponent` and `createBranchComponent` give the first parameter of their function as the props type. About 250 lines. First failing test: `a_chakra_factory_variant_key_is_an_own_prop`. Gate: core nextest; the census rows for Chakra's 11 and Spectrum's 4 factory components.

Depends on the collapse PR (it edits these three core files). About 250 lines. # Diagnosis: 437 Controls rows (A) and the @types/react recall drop (B)

Binary: the existing `oracle-run/target/release/caliper-docgen` (built from de016f69, not rebuilt). Source read at de016f69. Fixture: `sb-demo/src` itself (`Badge` = `ComponentProps<'span'> & {variant, asChild}`, `Button` = Chakra `ButtonProps & ComponentProps<'button'> & {...}`), `@types/react` and `@chakra-ui/react` installed in `sb-demo/node_modules`. Run: `extract --src sb-demo/src --json --no-cache` x checker on/off x `--html-attributes full|curated|none` x `--collapse-inherited-props dependencies|none` (12 runs, all exit 0).

Demo config checked first: `sb-demo/.storybook/main.ts` sets only `srcDirs`, `semanticWaitMs`, `prefetchStories`. No `collapseInheritedProps` and no `htmlAttributes`, so the defaults apply: `dependencies` and `full` (`packages/storybook/src/options.ts:40,43` pass `undefined` through; `crates/core/src/types/options.rs:47,196`).

## Measured (Button / Badge)

Rows = props + notableInherited, which is what `docgen_info` hands Storybook (`crates/core/src/pipeline/rdt.rs:63-72`). Layers are never expanded into rows.

- off (structural), full, dependencies: Button 439 props (289 from @types/react), Badge 281 (279 from @types/react). SystemProperties is a layer (706 names).
- on (checker), full, dependencies: Button 150 props (0 from @types/react, 130 Chakra `Conditions`), Badge 2. The element layers `React.ComponentProps[button]` and `[span]` have `totalProps 0` and no members.
- on or off, curated, dependencies: Button 150 + 164 notable = 314 rows, Badge 2 + 159 notable = 161.
- none: Button 150, Badge 2. Collapse `none` changes only SystemProperties (Button 853 props); it never changes the DOM props.

Storybook shows Button 437 and Badge 280. That is the structural full count (439 and 281) less `key`/`ref`/`children` that `arg-types.ts:12-20` and the RDT `children` rule drop. The CLI checker lane shows 150 and 2 for the same input. **The two checker lanes disagree on the same options.**

## A. 437 rows in Storybook

**Cause.** The session (Storybook) merge keeps every `@types/react` prop under `htmlAttributes: 'full'`. In `crates/core/src/react_types.rs:439-441`, `checker_prop_used` gives `HtmlAttributeMode::Full => true`, and it is applied in `crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs:338-341`. `react_props_wanted` (`react_types.rs:452-453`) asks the checker for all of them. Collapse never touches `@types/react`:

- `options.rs:89-90`: "A file in `node_modules` that is not a dependency's (`@types/react`, TypeScript's libraries) never collapses: React's attributes follow `htmlAttributes`."
- In the checker lane, `checker_sources` skips `react_declared` props (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs:715-716`).

The roughly 130 Chakra condition props (`_active`, `2xl`...) are listed because `Conditions` is not ambient by name (`crates/core/src/types/ambient.rs:101-105`: only `SystemProps`, `*StyleProps` and style prefixes). Its 130 props are under `LARGE_API_SOURCE` (200), so it is not collapsed (`options.rs:98-100`).

**Intended or regression: intended.** It was already so in 0.11.0. `caliper-docgen-core@0.11.0` has the same `Full => true` at `react_types.rs:440`, and the earlier 0.11.0 demo showed 1,141 rows. The default is documented in `options.rs:17-19`: "`Full`: actually resolve `@types/react`'s real ... interface chain, matching RDT's full ~250-300 attributes per element — the default." No recent PR (469, 476, 485, 483, 480) changed it. PR 469's collapse correctly removed the 705 SystemProperties rows (1,141 to 437).

The expectation "the DOM source is one layer with 8 notable props under `dependencies`" is not what any doc promises. The nearest mode, `curated`, keeps every `aria-*`, every non-Capture handler and the globals (`react_types.rs:415-418`), so it gives 164 notables, not 8.

**Effect on a Storybook user.** About 290 DOM, ARIA and event rows bury the roughly 20 real props. Badge (two own props) shows 280 rows.

**Smallest fix**, from smallest:

1. Config only. Default `htmlAttributes` to `'curated'` in the addon (`packages/storybook/src/options.ts:40`, and its docs in `packages/storybook/src/index.ts:6-12`). Button goes to 314 rows (measured), Badge to 161. This is a small change but not the expected shape.
2. Contract fix (recommended). When collapse is not `none`, treat `@types/react`'s element attributes as the ambient layer they already are by `is_dom_file`. List only `notable_html_attrs(element)` (17 names for `button`) as `notableInherited`, and leave the rest to the element layer. Files:
   - `crates/core/src/types/options.rs`: drop the "@types/react never collapses" exemption at :89-90 and :102, or add a React clause.
   - `crates/core/src/react_types.rs`: `checker_prop_used` / `react_props_wanted` take the collapse mode.
   - `crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`: `apply`, `target_of`.
   - The structural resolver's full-mode React expansion, so both lanes agree, plus a model test like `collapse_model.rs`.

   Button would show about 150 + 17 = **about 167 rows** (146 to 150 Chakra and own props, including the 130 conditions, plus the button notables). Badge would show 2 + span notables.

   Optionally, add Chakra's `Conditions` as a style source in `ambient.rs` (it is ambient, 130 > 30). Button would then drop to about 20 own + 17 notable = **about 37 rows**.

## B. @types/react recall about 0% with the checker on (CLI, collapse `none`)

**Cause.** The whole-project (CLI) merge drops every `react_declared` prop of a component that has any inheritance layer. In `crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs:429-437` (`apply_props`): `.filter(|prop| !prop.react_declared || (!layered && entry.props.contains_key(&prop.name)))`, followed by `Unanswered::Drop` (:439), which also removes the structural ones. The element layer is meant to "stand for them" (`crates/semantic/src/component.rs:33-37`). It ignores `htmlAttributes` and collapse, so `--collapse-inherited-props none` does not bring them back.

Antd (23.9%) and Spectrum (86.8%) are higher because many of their components have no element layer, and the `!layered` branch keeps React props the structural pass listed.

**Intended or regression: intended, and documented, since `d072b2ed` (2026-10-26, "merge the checker's props by name and apply htmlAttributes once after the merge").** That commit is in `caliper-docgen-core@0.8.0` through 0.11.0. 0.11.0 has the same filter at `semantic.rs:357-365`. B appeared in the weekly when 0.11.0 turned the checker on by default; it is not new in PRs 469 to 485. Docs that state it:

- `docs/type-checker-integration.md:66`: "Props `@types/react` declares are excluded by declaring file."
- `docs/type-checker-integration.md:203`: "With the whole-project merge, `@types/react`'s props stay with the inheritance layers as for any component, so the CLI shows the component's own props."
- `docs/measurement.md:256`: "`@types/react` props are counted apart (the whole-project checker pass leaves them out)."

The weekly's "@types/react props" recall column (`docs/measurement.md:94`) was not adapted. It still counts listed props, so it measures a removed feature.

**But it contradicts `htmlAttributes: 'full'`** (`options.rs:17-19`, "matching RDT's full ~250-300 attributes"). The layer that "stands for" them carries `totalProps: 0` and no member names, only `htmlElement`. A CLI JSON or `--format rdt` consumer therefore gets no DOM prop names unless it resolves the element itself. The session lane (A) does the opposite under the same option.

**Effect on a Storybook user: none.** The addon goes through the session lane (`semantic_hook.rs`), not `apply_props`. The effect is on CLI and RDT-format consumers and on the weekly metric.

**Smallest fix.** Pick one contract for both lanes; the one described under A, fix 2, settles both. On its own:

- (a) Metric only: in `scripts/weekly.py`, count an `@types/react` RDT prop as recalled when the component has an element layer for that element (or report the column only for `--no-checker`). One file. No output change.
- (b) Output: make `apply_props` (`semantic.rs:429-437`) filter with `react_types::checker_prop_used(mode, ...)` as the session does. That restores full-mode recall to about 99%, and Chakra's CLI Button to 439. Files: `crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs` (`apply_props`, `merge_semantic` needs the mode), `crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs:169` (passes it), and the CLI's target building so `react_wanted` is `None` under `full`.

Not run: a bisect (not needed: the 0.11.0 tag has both policies), and the Chakra corpus Button in the CLI (the report already has 146 + layer there). No repo files changed.
# Findings synthesis (trails 404/405, ~50 Entire findings, 2026-11-15)

Why reviewers keep finding things: every finding is an instance of one of eight classes. Each fix so far closed the
instance, not the class, and most guards are DENY-lists (enumerate what is wrong) where the rule needs an ALLOW-list
(enumerate what is proven, decline the rest). A deny-list is complete only until the next grammar form: the newest
finding (273: `Partial<Config>` with a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) is the same class as the six before it.

| # | Class (semantic invariant that was broken) | Findings (change) | Class-level remedy |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Silence is not evidence: absent data was treated as 'complete/none' | declare fn = complete empty body, optional-chain computed member (268); alias Pick over checker-only source collapses (267 x6); name-only filter hides another source's prop (277); `used` empty (281) | Unknown is the default state; Complete is earned. Exhaustive `match` on node/type kinds, no wildcard arm, the default arm is `Unknown`/`Declined`. One rule in the one decision function: not proven => keep listed. |
| C2 | Lossy model asserted exactness (deny-list guard) | Omit/keyof index sig, Array shadow, scope, Partial<Dict>, readonly, Required undefined (273), Symbol.iterator key (273 new) | ALLOW-list expansion: expand only members of a closed set of simple forms (identifier or string-literal key, plain/optional/readonly known, non-generic), decline everything else. Oracle generator iterates the GRAMMAR of member/key forms, not the findings. |
| C3 | Spelling used where binding is required | JSX usage by name, builtin `Array` by spelling, shadowed tags, AtFile scope, three path predicates for ambient/React | Resolve by binding or return unknown; one `declaration_origin`; no string equality on identifiers in decisions. |
| C4 | Derived state outside the dependency model | stale watch/lazy relevance (281), call-site cache, scheduler re-ask after edit (279/282) | Everything an answer reads is recorded (`deps`) or the answer is not kept; `watch_equals_fresh` model with mutation proof per dependency kind. |
| C5 | One decision, two owners | collapse lanes (267, 4 rounds), picked keys (4 readers), `annotate` x3, `{...props}` meaning, relevance map vs ADR | One function, one sink, provenance `(source, key, how)` not counts/names; lanes feed inputs, never decide. |
| C6 | Host assumptions | cgroup v1 mount (272) | Read the system's own description (mountinfo); fall back loudly. Fixed. |
| C7 | Hand-tuned policy without a reference model | scheduler fairness/starvation (279/281) | Property test against a reference model (sort by class, arrival) with the starvation rule as the spec. |
| C8 | Contract drift: code, ADR, schema disagree; fields defined but never populated | schema 8 per-component map vs ADR `used`, dead story-args, `used` empty on corpora, 281 | ADR is the contract; a field ships only with a producer, a consumer and a corpus count that is non-zero. |

3	
4	**Status:** Proposed **Date:** 2026-11-15
5	
6	## Context
7	
8	Every surface returns every prop the checker resolves, minus what a collapsed layer hides. That is useless to Storybook and to agents: Chakra's `Button` had about 1,141 argTypes before the collapse-by-relevance PR (`feat/collapse-large-sources-by-default`) and 146 after it, and the rows still hidden are the ones consumers pass. Measured on origin/main 7b8f6d0d with the checker (trail 405 T5, `caliper-fixtures/shrink/relevance-baseline.md`), the share of the props a component's call sites pass that the output lists is 0.43 on shadcn (mean over 408 components; median 0.50), 0.86 on Mantine, 0.91 on ant-design and 0.96 on react-spectrum. Nearly every miss is a DOM attribute in a collapsed `React.ComponentProps<"el">` layer (shadcn: `className` alone on 243 components), and those layers carry `htmlElement` with no `members` and `totalProps` 0, so a reader cannot tell what is inside them. Today's choices come from size and from name lists (`resolver/ambient.rs`'s `*StyleProps`, `GlobalDOMEvents` clauses; `notable_html_attrs` in `react_types.rs:462`), which the owner rules out.
9	
10	The checker's cost follows what it converts, not what is shown. A whole-project `extract` of Chakra's own repository built 42 GB of `PropType` trees converting its style system (`shrink/chakra-memory.md`), and the only memory guard (`OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`, `crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs:93`) reads the checker's arenas (`crates/semantic/src/checker.rs:169`), not the converter's heap, and only between requests (`on_demand.rs:643`).
11	
12	## Decision
13	
14	### A. Relevance decides what is shown, from evidence
15	
16	The owner's rules: returning all resolved props is useless for Storybook and agents; relevance decides what to show; it is derived from evidence, with no name lists; agent output is narrowed later.
17	
18	**Signals.** Each prop a component's props type reaches gets evidence from four places.
19	
20	- **The props type.** A member the props type declares itself is always shown. So is each key of `Pick<X, 'a' | 'b'>`, named on purpose; `Omit<X, 'k'>` says only that `k` is gone, nothing about the rest. A member that redeclares or narrows a base member is the component's own. A required member is shown (a story cannot render without it), and so is one with a `@default` tag or a destructuring default in the body (the component handles it). JSDoc and a literal-union type do not show a member on their own: as promoters they would list every documented member of a style system; they order the shown rows (open question 1).
21	- **Spreads in the body** (T1's `ComponentMapping::body`). `{...rest}` on a DOM tag passes the ambient DOM attributes: no evidence, ignored. A spread onto a component is one hop to that component's own non-ambient props, with the JSX tag resolved to the component by symbol and import (ADR 0027's identity, never the display name). An attribute set after the spread is fixed and subtracted; one set before it is an overridable default and kept; an attribute whose value is one of the component's own props adds nothing. A name in `reads` is shown when its source is not ambient.
22	- **Call sites.** The props consumers pass at JSX usages across the project (T1's `SourceData::jsx_usages`) and in stories' `args`, counted per component with a floor of `max(2, 20%)` of its sites. The baseline puts the cost at 0.30 (Mantine), 0.03 (Spectrum), 0.76 (shadcn) and 0.24 (antd) extra entries per component.
23	- **Unknown.** When `handed_on` is true, `reads` is incomplete (T1's contract), and the body says nothing: never guessed. The member falls back to today's single collapse decision with the reaching count (`CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` in the collapse PR; on main it is still `ResolutionContext::collapses`, `resolver/mod.rs:595`, by declared count, so `decide` is wired only after that PR merges), so missing evidence never hides more than today.
24	
25	**Ambient** is decided by where a member is declared, not by its name: a member `@types/react` declares (by declaring path, as `is_react_declared` in `crates/semantic/src/component.rs` recognizes React terminals), or one that reaches the component only through a spread onto a DOM tag. Each lane computes the bit for each prop and hands it to `decide` in `Evidence` (`is_react_declared` is private to `caliper-docgen-semantic`, which core does not depend on); `decide` never recomputes it, and a model test in the style of the collapse PR's `collapse_model.rs` holds the two lanes to the same bits. `ambient.rs`'s name clauses and `notable_html_attrs` stay as the unknown-evidence fallback until the T5 gate shows evidence replaces them; then they are deleted (slice R9).
26	
27	**Combination.** One function, `relevance::decide(&Evidence) -> Shown`, owns it, as `CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` owns collapsing; both lanes and every surface call it.
28	
29	- Shown as a row: own, picked, overriding, required, defaulted; a non-ambient member that is forwarded, read, or passed at the floor.
30	- Named in the layer's `used` list: an ambient member passed at the floor or read in the body.
31	- Left in a collapsed layer: everything else with complete evidence, even from a source today's rule lists (its source becomes a layer). A non-ambient member with unknown body evidence and no other signal is listed or collapsed as today.
32	
33	**Output.** A collapsed `InheritedLayer` (`crates/core/src/types/output.rs:83`) gains `used`: the names of its members that evidence put forward, written once as a name list (ADR 0018), not as typed rows. Universal props such as `className`, `style` and `id` cost a name each instead of a row each. A `React.ComponentProps<"el">` layer also gets its `members`, so a reader can check `used` against it. No per-prop flag in this ADR: the row/layer split already says shown or not, and why a row is shown is for the agent output, deferred. `SCHEMA_VERSION` goes from 7 to 8 (ADR 0017), with the RDT view, the JSON schema, `binding.d.ts` and a changeset.
34	
35	**Consumers.** The Storybook addon makes argTypes from rows, then one name-only row per `used` name with the layer as its category; an option (`relevance: 'all'`) asks for the expanded output, which is today's `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'`. CLI JSON and TOON carry the same output. Agent output keeps its current form until the agent flow is narrowed.
36	
37	**Acceptance gate** (T5's metric, ported into the weekly by T4). Coverage counts a passed prop as visible when it is a row or in `used`. Call-site evidence is computed from half of the files (by path hash) and coverage is measured on the other half, so the gate does not pass by construction. On the half the floor is `max(1, 20%)`, and only components with at least 6 sites are measured, so the gate does not test a stricter rule than the one shipped.
38	
39	- Coverage mean rises: shadcn 0.43 to at least 0.70; Mantine 0.86 to at least 0.88; antd 0.91 to at least 0.93; Spectrum stays at least 0.96.
40	- Rows shown fall: the median rows per component does not rise on any corpus (Mantine 77, Spectrum 74, shadcn 3, antd 17), and total rows fall on Mantine and Spectrum. Chakra `Button`'s typed rows stay at or under 146 (its `used` names come on top and are reported apart).
41	- These targets are proposals. Only the extra-entry costs above were measured; the fall in rows is not predicted.
42	
43	### B. The checker is scheduled by the props that will be shown
44	
45	The owner asked for a queue. Its parts, against what exists:
46	
47	- **Item.** The props of one component that relevance will show, at one revision, not the whole component; collapsed members are listed by name and parent and never converted. Exists: `SemanticTarget::react_wanted` and `described` (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs:169-175`) already narrow what one target converts. New: a `shown` set from `relevance::decide`.
48	- **Priority classes**, on-screen > neighbouring stories > background fill. Exists: two (`Priority::Interactive` and `Background`, `types/semantic.rs:221`), two lanes with a starvation bound and raising (`Queue`, `on_demand.rs:150-199`, `INTERACTIVE_STREAK` 4), a raise when an on-screen request joins a queued one (`pipeline/semantic_hook.rs:256`). The addon's prefetch queue holds the next `prefetchStories - 1` stories, replaced on every selection (`packages/storybook/src/background.ts:39`, `preset.ts:150`, `prefetch.ts:32`), one story at a time (`background.ts:81-89`), and asks at `Background` (`pipeline/watch.rs:464`). 49	- **Preemption and cancel.** Exists: an edit forgets every kept and pending answer in the hook (`semantic_hook.rs:180`); the lifecycle reducer refreshes an answer superseded by an edit (`lifecycle.ts:196`); navigation replaces the addon's queue. Missing: nothing reaches `OnDemand`'s queue, which has no cancel, so requests nobody waits for still run. New: a request carries a cancel token tripped by an edit or by the navigation that replaced it, dropped when taken. Raising a request clears its token: an on-screen request that joined a queued prefetch (`Found::Joined`, `semantic_hook.rs:256`) is waited for, so a navigation never cancels it; and preemption between components of one request (a tsrs call cannot be interrupted).

New: the worker takes the queued items of one class together and roots one snapshot at the union of their roots, so they share the program and one converter memo; the memo is dropped with that snapshot, never carried to an updated or re-rooted one (type ids are valid within one snapshot, ADR 0026). New: the scheduler admits a background item only under a soft budget read from the allocator, holds background work above it, and stops the checker above the hard one, as `stop_past_bound` does.
52	- **Stream each result.** Exists: one `Delivery` per request (`types/semantic.rs:256`), and the reducer turns each settled key into a refresh (`lifecycle.ts:185-205`, invariants 1 to 6). New: a request of several keys delivers each key when converted. The CLI keeps one write: canonical JSON interns props across components (ADR 0009, 0018).
53	
54	Not determined: whether tsrs's memory allows the converter memo to live as long as a snapshot over a long session (ADR 0026 measured 98 to 246 MB over 150 edits without it); whether `mi_process_info` reads the same under the napi host; how far listing collapsed members without converting them lowers the 42 GB case, since the collapse PR collapses `SystemProperties` after conversion.

171	
172	Why reviewers keep finding things: every finding is an instance of one of eight classes. Each fix so far closed the
173	instance, not the class, and most guards are DENY-lists (enumerate what is wrong) where the rule needs an ALLOW-list
174	(enumerate what is proven, decline the rest). A deny-list is complete only until the next grammar form: the newest

176	
177	| # | Class (semantic invariant that was broken) | Findings (change) | Class-level remedy |
178	|---|---|---|---|
179	| C1 | Silence is not evidence: absent data was treated as 'complete/none' | declare fn = complete empty body, optional-chain computed member (268); alias Pick over checker-only source collapses (267 x6); name-only filter hides another source's prop (277); `used` empty (281) | Unknown is the default state; Complete is earned. Exhaustive `match` on node/type kinds, no wildcard arm, the default arm is `Unknown`/`Declined`. One rule in the one decision function: not proven => keep listed. |
180	| C2 | Lossy model asserted exactness (deny-list guard) | Omit/keyof index sig, Array shadow, scope, Partial<Dict>, readonly, Required undefined (273), Symbol.iterator key (273 new) | ALLOW-list expansion: expand only members of a closed set of simple forms (identifier or string-literal key, plain/optional/readonly known, non-generic), decline everything else. Oracle generator iterates the GRAMMAR of member/key forms, not the findings. |
181	| C3 | Spelling used where binding is required | JSX usage by name, builtin `Array` by spelling, shadowed tags, AtFile scope, three path predicates for ambient/React | Resolve by binding or return unknown; one `declaration_origin`; no string equality on identifiers in decisions. |

183	| C5 | One decision, two owners | collapse lanes (267, 4 rounds), picked keys (4 readers), `annotate` x3, `{...props}` meaning, relevance map vs ADR | One function, one sink, provenance `(source, key, how)` not counts/names; lanes feed inputs, never decide. |
184	| C6 | Host assumptions | cgroup v1 mount (272) | Read the system's own description (mountinfo); fall back loudly. Fixed. |
185	| C7 | Hand-tuned policy without a reference model | scheduler fairness/starvation (279/281) | Property test against a reference model (sort by class, arrival) with the starvation rule as the spec. |
186	| C8 | Contract drift: code, ADR, schema disagree; fields defined but never populated | schema 8 per-component map vs ADR `used`, dead story-args, `used` empty on corpora, 281 | ADR is the contract; a field ships only with a producer, a consumer and a corpus count that is non-zero. |
187	
188	Plus a process class: stacked PRs show the same code in every child (about 40% of the raw count) and merge commits
189	re-expose it. Remedy: merge in order, review once, retarget children.

191	## Pre-push gate (every slice, before the Entire reviewer ever sees it)
192	
193	1. Invariants: write the 3 to 6 invariants of the slice in the PR body in these terms: 'unknown unless proven',
194	   'resolved by binding', 'every read recorded', 'one owner', 'wired or not defined'.
195	2. Grammar sweep: list every syntactic or type form the touched code can receive (all AST node kinds, all member
196	   and key forms, all declaration kinds) and show each one is handled or lands in the Unknown/Declined arm, by an
197	   EXHAUSTIVE match (no `_ =>`) or a generated test over the grammar with the oracle (checker, TS API) as judge.

200	   must try to produce a wrong output (not read the diff for style). Fix once, at the class level.

202	# Worker contract (caliper). Read once; the brief only names the task, the files you own and the call cap.
203	
204	Scope
205	- Edit only the files the brief names. If another file must change, stop and say which and why.
206	- Never ask the user questions. If blocked, report what blocks and what you tried. Do not wait on background work: finish or report.

208	Branch and push

210	- Rust 1.99.1 on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin) for builds; commits need MISE_RUST_VERSION=1.99.1 (the mise shim forces 1.98.1). 217	- Tests that fail on base for every behavior change. No oracle runs, no corpus fetches. No new scripts, options or recipes. Changeset only if `just semver` demands one.
218	- No wall-clock timing unless the brief asks; check `uptime`, and prefer allocation or instruction counts (load-independent).
219	
220	Cap
221	- Stop and report after the call cap in the brief (default 60 tool calls) with what you have verified. Listing something as 'not done' with its cause beats burning more calls.
222	
223	Artifacts (agents to agents; humans see them at the edge)
224	- Write the PR body to ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/<branch, slashes as dashes>.md: `## What`, `## Evidence` (numbers, exit codes, what was diffed), `## Not verified`, last line `https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`. The lead publishes it unedited.
225	- Final message <= 120 words: branch, head SHA (ls-remote verified), body path, blockers. Nothing else.

228	- Guards are ALLOW-lists: handle a closed set of proven forms, everything else is Unknown/Declined (never 'complete', never 'none', never 'exact'). No `_ =>` arms in decisions over node/type kinds.

# 0028. Show the props evidence makes relevant, and schedule the checker by what will be shown

**Status:** Proposed **Date:** 2026-11-15

## Context

Every surface returns every prop the checker resolves, minus what a collapsed layer hides. That is useless to Storybook and to agents: Chakra's `Button` had about 1,141 argTypes before the collapse-by-relevance PR (`feat/collapse-large-sources-by-default`) and 146 after it, and the rows still hidden are the ones consumers pass. Measured on origin/main 7b8f6d0d with the checker (trail 405 T5, `caliper-fixtures/shrink/relevance-baseline.md`), the share of the props a component's call sites pass that the output lists is 0.43 on shadcn (mean over 408 components; median 0.50), 0.86 on Mantine, 0.91 on ant-design and 0.96 on react-spectrum. Nearly every miss is a DOM attribute in a collapsed `React.ComponentProps<"el">` layer (shadcn: `className` alone on 243 components), and those layers carry `htmlElement` with no `members` and `totalProps` 0, so a reader cannot tell what is inside them. Today's choices come from size and from name lists (`resolver/ambient.rs`'s `*StyleProps`, `GlobalDOMEvents` clauses; `notable_html_attrs` in `react_types.rs:462`), which the owner rules out.

The checker's cost follows what it converts, not what is shown. A whole-project `extract` of Chakra's own repository built 42 GB of `PropType` trees converting its style system (`shrink/chakra-memory.md`), and the only memory guard (`OnDemandConfig::max_rss_mib`, `crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs:93`) reads the checker's arenas (`crates/semantic/src/checker.rs:169`), not the converter's heap, and only between requests (`on_demand.rs:643`).

## Decision

### A. Relevance decides what is shown, from evidence

The owner's rules: returning all resolved props is useless for Storybook and agents; relevance decides what to show; it is derived from evidence, with no name lists; agent output is narrowed later.

**Signals.** Each prop a component's props type reaches gets evidence from four places.

- **The props type.** A member the props type declares itself is always shown. So is each key of `Pick<X, 'a' | 'b'>`, named on purpose; `Omit<X, 'k'>` says only that `k` is gone, nothing about the rest. A member that redeclares or narrows a base member is the component's own. A required member is shown (a story cannot render without it), and so is one with a `@default` tag or a destructuring default in the body (the component handles it). JSDoc and a literal-union type do not show a member on their own: as promoters they would list every documented member of a style system; they order the shown rows (open question 1).
- **Spreads in the body** (T1's `ComponentMapping::body`). `{...rest}` on a DOM tag passes the ambient DOM attributes: no evidence, ignored. A spread onto a component is one hop to that component's own non-ambient props, with the JSX tag resolved to the component by symbol and import (ADR 0027's identity, never the display name). An attribute set after the spread is fixed and subtracted; one set before it is an overridable default and kept; an attribute whose value is one of the component's own props adds nothing. A name in `reads` is shown when its source is not ambient.
- **Call sites.** The props consumers pass at JSX usages across the project (T1's `SourceData::jsx_usages`) and in stories' `args`, counted per component with a floor of `max(2, 20%)` of its sites. The baseline puts the cost at 0.30 (Mantine), 0.03 (Spectrum), 0.76 (shadcn) and 0.24 (antd) extra entries per component.
- **Unknown.** When `handed_on` is true, `reads` is incomplete (T1's contract), and the body says nothing: never guessed. The member falls back to today's single collapse decision with the reaching count (`CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` in the collapse PR; on main it is still `ResolutionContext::collapses`, `resolver/mod.rs:595`, by declared count, so `decide` is wired only after that PR merges), so missing evidence never hides more than today.

**Ambient** is decided by where a member is declared, not by its name: a member `@types/react` declares (by declaring path, as `is_react_declared` in `crates/semantic/src/component.rs` recognizes React terminals), or one that reaches the component only through a spread onto a DOM tag. Each lane computes the bit for each prop and hands it to `decide` in `Evidence` (`is_react_declared` is private to `caliper-docgen-semantic`, which core does not depend on); `decide` never recomputes it, and a model test in the style of the collapse PR's `collapse_model.rs` holds the two lanes to the same bits. `ambient.rs`'s name clauses and `notable_html_attrs` stay as the unknown-evidence fallback until the T5 gate shows evidence replaces them; then they are deleted (slice R9).

**Combination.** One function, `relevance::decide(&Evidence) -> Shown`, owns it, as `CollapseInheritedProps::collapses` owns collapsing; both lanes and every surface call it.

- Shown as a row: own, picked, overriding, required, defaulted; a non-ambient member that is forwarded, read, or passed at the floor.
- Named in the layer's `used` list: an ambient member passed at the floor or read in the body.
- Left in a collapsed layer: everything else with complete evidence, even from a source today's rule lists (its source becomes a layer). A non-ambient member with unknown body evidence and no other signal is listed or collapsed as today.

**Output.** A collapsed `InheritedLayer` (`crates/core/src/types/output.rs:83`) gains `used`: the names of its members that evidence put forward, written once as a name list (ADR 0018), not as typed rows. Universal props such as `className`, `style` and `id` cost a name each instead of a row each. A `React.ComponentProps<"el">` layer also gets its `members`, so a reader can check `used` against it. No per-prop flag in this ADR: the row/layer split already says shown or not, and why a row is shown is for the agent output, deferred. `SCHEMA_VERSION` goes from 7 to 8 (ADR 0017), with the RDT view, the JSON schema, `binding.d.ts` and a changeset.

**Consumers.** The Storybook addon makes argTypes from rows, then one name-only row per `used` name with the layer as its category; an option (`relevance: 'all'`) asks for the expanded output, which is today's `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'`. CLI JSON and TOON carry the same output. Agent output keeps its current form until the agent flow is narrowed.

**Acceptance gate** (T5's metric, ported into the weekly by T4). Coverage counts a passed prop as visible when it is a row or in `used`. Call-site evidence is computed from half of the files (by path hash) and coverage is measured on the other half, so the gate does not pass by construction. On the half the floor is `max(1, 20%)`, and only components with at least 6 sites are measured, so the gate does not test a stricter rule than the one shipped.

- Coverage mean rises: shadcn 0.43 to at least 0.70; Mantine 0.86 to at least 0.88; antd 0.91 to at least 0.93; Spectrum stays at least 0.96.
- Rows shown fall: the median rows per component does not rise on any corpus (Mantine 77, Spectrum 74, shadcn 3, antd 17), and total rows fall on Mantine and Spectrum. Chakra `Button`'s typed rows stay at or under 146 (its `used` names come on top and are reported apart).

### B. The checker is scheduled by the props that will be shown

The owner asked for a queue. Its parts, against what exists:

- **Item.** The props of one component that relevance will show, at one revision, not the whole component; collapsed members are listed by name and parent and never converted. Exists: `SemanticTarget::react_wanted` and `described` (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs:169-175`) already narrow what one target converts. New: a `shown` set from `relevance::decide`.
- **Priority classes**, on-screen > neighbouring stories > background fill. Exists: two (`Priority::Interactive` and `Background`, `types/semantic.rs:221`), two lanes with a starvation bound and raising (`Queue`, `on_demand.rs:150-199`, `INTERACTIVE_STREAK` 4), a raise when an on-screen request joins a queued one (`pipeline/semantic_hook.rs:256`). The addon's prefetch queue holds the next `prefetchStories - 1` stories, replaced on every selection (`packages/storybook/src/background.ts:39`, `preset.ts:150`, `prefetch.ts:32`), one story at a time (`background.ts:81-89`), and asks at `Background` (`pipeline/watch.rs:464`). New: a third class, `Neighbour`, between them.
- **Preemption and cancel.** Exists: an edit forgets every kept and pending answer in the hook (`semantic_hook.rs:180`); the lifecycle reducer refreshes an answer superseded by an edit (`lifecycle.ts:196`); navigation replaces the addon's queue. Missing: nothing reaches `OnDemand`'s queue, which has no cancel, so requests nobody waits for still run. New: a request carries a cancel token tripped by an edit or by the navigation that replaced it, dropped when taken. Raising a request clears its token: an on-screen request that joined a queued prefetch (`Found::Joined`, `semantic_hook.rs:256`) is waited for, so a navigation never cancels it; and preemption between components of one request (a tsrs call cannot be interrupted).
- **Batching by snapshot.** Exists: `OnDemand` keeps one snapshot and re-roots it per request (`Checker::snapshot_for`, `on_demand.rs:551`); the one-shot CLI answers every component on one program with eight files in flight sharing one converter (`crates/semantic/src/lib.rs:49`, `session`). A request whose roots differ re-roots the snapshot (`rerooted`, `on_demand.rs:574`), which makes a new one with new type ids. New: the worker takes the queued items of one class together and roots one snapshot at the union of their roots, so they share the program and one converter memo; the memo is dropped with that snapshot, never carried to an updated or re-rooted one (type ids are valid within one snapshot, ADR 0026). The memo is per request today.
- **Admission on a memory budget.** Exists: the arena guard (`Upkeep::decide`, `on_demand.rs:709`), which misses the converter heap. In flight: the one-shot heap budget (heap-budget slice B, branch `feat/one-shot-heap-budget`, no commits yet), counting converted nodes inside conversion. New: the scheduler admits a background item only under a soft budget read from the allocator, holds background work above it, and stops the checker above the hard one, as `stop_past_bound` does.
- **Stream each result.** Exists: one `Delivery` per request (`types/semantic.rs:256`), and the reducer turns each settled key into a refresh (`lifecycle.ts:185-205`, invariants 1 to 6). New: a request of several keys delivers each key when converted. The CLI keeps one write: canonical JSON interns props across components (ADR 0009, 0018).

Not determined: whether tsrs's memory allows the converter memo to live as long as a snapshot over a long session (ADR 0026 measured 98 to 246 MB over 150 edits without it); whether `mi_process_info` reads the same under the napi host; how far listing collapsed members without converting them lowers the 42 GB case, since the collapse PR collapses `SystemProperties` after conversion.

## Consequences

- Output changes on every surface; the addon's default argTypes change again after the collapse PR. Complete evidence hides on purpose props today lists (a 10-prop dependency source the body never reads becomes a layer); that is how rows fall. Only a prop with unknown evidence is guaranteed to be shown as today.
- Agents read the same narrowed output until their flow is designed.
- Call-site evidence makes a component's answer depend on other files. Watch and the kept answer must invalidate on a consumer's edit, and the per-component closure is still unknown (ADR 0026), so invalidation stays whole-project.
- The scheduler adds a third class, cancel tokens and a long-lived memo to `OnDemand`; its determinism gate (gate harness) must hold with cancels.
- Breaking for readers of `InheritedLayer` (schema 8).

## Alternatives considered

- **A fixed universal set** (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `ref` plus handlers): about the same 1 to 3 rows, but a name list.
- **Expand everything** (`none`): 280 to 1,100 rows per component (`--no-checker` figures in the baseline).
- **Whole components as queue items**: converts collapsed members nobody sees, which is where the Chakra memory went.

# Diagnosis: 437 Controls rows (A) and the @types/react recall drop (B)

Binary: the existing `oracle-run/target/release/caliper-docgen` (built from de016f69, not rebuilt). Source read at de016f69. Fixture: `sb-demo/src` itself (`Badge` = `ComponentProps<'span'> & {variant, asChild}`, `Button` = Chakra `ButtonProps & ComponentProps<'button'> & {...}`), `@types/react` and `@chakra-ui/react` installed in `sb-demo/node_modules`. Run: `extract --src sb-demo/src --json --no-cache` x checker on/off x `--html-attributes full|curated|none` x `--collapse-inherited-props dependencies|none` (12 runs, all exit 0).

Demo config checked first: `sb-demo/.storybook/main.ts` sets only `srcDirs`, `semanticWaitMs`, `prefetchStories`. No `collapseInheritedProps` and no `htmlAttributes`, so the defaults apply: `dependencies` and `full` (`packages/storybook/src/options.ts:40,43` pass `undefined` through; `crates/core/src/types/options.rs:47,196`).

## Measured (Button / Badge)

Rows = props + notableInherited, which is what `docgen_info` hands Storybook (`crates/core/src/pipeline/rdt.rs:63-72`). Layers are never expanded into rows.

- off (structural), full, dependencies: Button 439 props (289 from @types/react), Badge 281 (279 from @types/react). SystemProperties is a layer (706 names).
- on (checker), full, dependencies: Button 150 props (0 from @types/react, 130 Chakra `Conditions`), Badge 2. The element layers `React.ComponentProps[button]` and `[span]` have `totalProps 0` and no members.
- on or off, curated, dependencies: Button 150 + 164 notable = 314 rows, Badge 2 + 159 notable = 161.
- none: Button 150, Badge 2. Collapse `none` changes only SystemProperties (Button 853 props); it never changes the DOM props.

Storybook shows Button 437 and Badge 280. That is the structural full count (439 and 281) less `key`/`ref`/`children` that `arg-types.ts:12-20` and the RDT `children` rule drop. The CLI checker lane shows 150 and 2 for the same input. **The two checker lanes disagree on the same options.**

## A. 437 rows in Storybook

**Cause.** The session (Storybook) merge keeps every `@types/react` prop under `htmlAttributes: 'full'`. In `crates/core/src/react_types.rs:439-441`, `checker_prop_used` gives `HtmlAttributeMode::Full => true`, and it is applied in `crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs:338-341`. `react_props_wanted` (`react_types.rs:452-453`) asks the checker for all of them. Collapse never touches `@types/react`:

- `options.rs:89-90`: "A file in `node_modules` that is not a dependency's (`@types/react`, TypeScript's libraries) never collapses: React's attributes follow `htmlAttributes`."
- In the checker lane, `checker_sources` skips `react_declared` props (`crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs:715-716`).

The roughly 130 Chakra condition props (`_active`, `2xl`...) are listed because `Conditions` is not ambient by name (`crates/core/src/types/ambient.rs:101-105`: only `SystemProps`, `*StyleProps` and style prefixes). Its 130 props are under `LARGE_API_SOURCE` (200), so it is not collapsed (`options.rs:98-100`).

**Intended or regression: intended.** It was already so in 0.11.0. `caliper-docgen-core@0.11.0` has the same `Full => true` at `react_types.rs:440`, and the earlier 0.11.0 demo showed 1,141 rows. The default is documented in `options.rs:17-19`: "`Full`: actually resolve `@types/react`'s real ... interface chain, matching RDT's full ~250-300 attributes per element — the default." No recent PR (469, 476, 485, 483, 480) changed it. PR 469's collapse correctly removed the 705 SystemProperties rows (1,141 to 437).

The expectation "the DOM source is one layer with 8 notable props under `dependencies`" is not what any doc promises. The nearest mode, `curated`, keeps every `aria-*`, every non-Capture handler and the globals (`react_types.rs:415-418`), so it gives 164 notables, not 8.

**Effect on a Storybook user.** About 290 DOM, ARIA and event rows bury the roughly 20 real props. Badge (two own props) shows 280 rows.

**Smallest fix**, from smallest:

1. Config only. Default `htmlAttributes` to `'curated'` in the addon (`packages/storybook/src/options.ts:40`, and its docs in `packages/storybook/src/index.ts:6-12`). Button goes to 314 rows (measured), Badge to 161. This is a small change but not the expected shape.
2. Contract fix (recommended). When collapse is not `none`, treat `@types/react`'s element attributes as the ambient layer they already are by `is_dom_file`. List only `notable_html_attrs(element)` (17 names for `button`) as `notableInherited`, and leave the rest to the element layer. Files:
   - `crates/core/src/types/options.rs`: drop the "@types/react never collapses" exemption at :89-90 and :102, or add a React clause.
   - `crates/core/src/react_types.rs`: `checker_prop_used` / `react_props_wanted` take the collapse mode.
   - `crates/core/src/pipeline/semantic_hook.rs`: `apply`, `target_of`.
   - The structural resolver's full-mode React expansion, so both lanes agree, plus a model test like `collapse_model.rs`.

   Button would show about 150 + 17 = **about 167 rows** (146 to 150 Chakra and own props, including the 130 conditions, plus the button notables). Badge would show 2 + span notables.

   Optionally, add Chakra's `Conditions` as a style source in `ambient.rs` (it is ambient, 130 > 30). Button would then drop to about 20 own + 17 notable = **about 37 rows**.

## B. @types/react recall about 0% with the checker on (CLI, collapse `none`)

**Cause.** The whole-project (CLI) merge drops every `react_declared` prop of a component that has any inheritance layer. In `crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs:429-437` (`apply_props`): `.filter(|prop| !prop.react_declared || (!layered && entry.props.contains_key(&prop.name)))`, followed by `Unanswered::Drop` (:439), which also removes the structural ones. The element layer is meant to "stand for them" (`crates/semantic/src/component.rs:33-37`). It ignores `htmlAttributes` and collapse, so `--collapse-inherited-props none` does not bring them back.

Antd (23.9%) and Spectrum (86.8%) are higher because many of their components have no element layer, and the `!layered` branch keeps React props the structural pass listed.

**Intended or regression: intended, and documented, since `d072b2ed` (2026-10-26, "merge the checker's props by name and apply htmlAttributes once after the merge").** That commit is in `caliper-docgen-core@0.8.0` through 0.11.0. 0.11.0 has the same filter at `semantic.rs:357-365`. B appeared in the weekly when 0.11.0 turned the checker on by default; it is not new in PRs 469 to 485. Docs that state it:

- `docs/type-checker-integration.md:66`: "Props `@types/react` declares are excluded by declaring file."
- `docs/type-checker-integration.md:203`: "With the whole-project merge, `@types/react`'s props stay with the inheritance layers as for any component, so the CLI shows the component's own props."
- `docs/measurement.md:256`: "`@types/react` props are counted apart (the whole-project checker pass leaves them out)."

The weekly's "@types/react props" recall column (`docs/measurement.md:94`) was not adapted. It still counts listed props, so it measures a removed feature.

**But it contradicts `htmlAttributes: 'full'`** (`options.rs:17-19`, "matching RDT's full ~250-300 attributes"). The layer that "stands for" them carries `totalProps: 0` and no member names, only `htmlElement`. A CLI JSON or `--format rdt` consumer therefore gets no DOM prop names unless it resolves the element itself. The session lane (A) does the opposite under the same option.

**Effect on a Storybook user: none.** The addon goes through the session lane (`semantic_hook.rs`), not `apply_props`. The effect is on CLI and RDT-format consumers and on the weekly metric.

**Smallest fix.** Pick one contract for both lanes; the one described under A, fix 2, settles both. On its own:

- (a) Metric only: in `scripts/weekly.py`, count an `@types/react` RDT prop as recalled when the component has an element layer for that element (or report the column only for `--no-checker`). One file. No output change.
- (b) Output: make `apply_props` (`semantic.rs:429-437`) filter with `react_types::checker_prop_used(mode, ...)` as the session does. That restores full-mode recall to about 99%, and Chakra's CLI Button to 439. Files: `crates/core/src/types/semantic.rs` (`apply_props`, `merge_semantic` needs the mode), `crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs:169` (passes it), and the CLI's target building so `react_wanted` is `None` under `full`.

Not run: a bisect (not needed: the 0.11.0 tag has both policies), and the Chakra corpus Button in the CLI (the report already has 146 + layer there). No repo files changed.
# Findings synthesis (trails 404/405, ~50 Entire findings, 2026-11-15)

Why reviewers keep finding things: every finding is an instance of one of eight classes. Each fix so far closed the
instance, not the class, and most guards are DENY-lists (enumerate what is wrong) where the rule needs an ALLOW-list
(enumerate what is proven, decline the rest). A deny-list is complete only until the next grammar form: the newest
finding (273: `Partial<Config>` with a `[Symbol.iterator]` key) is the same class as the six before it.

| # | Class (semantic invariant that was broken) | Findings (change) | Class-level remedy |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | Silence is not evidence: absent data was treated as 'complete/none' | declare fn = complete empty body, optional-chain computed member (268); alias Pick over checker-only source collapses (267 x6); name-only filter hides another source's prop (277); `used` empty (281) | Unknown is the default state; Complete is earned. Exhaustive `match` on node/type kinds, no wildcard arm, the default arm is `Unknown`/`Declined`. One rule in the one decision function: not proven => keep listed. |
| C2 | Lossy model asserted exactness (deny-list guard) | Omit/keyof index sig, Array shadow, scope, Partial<Dict>, readonly, Required undefined (273), Symbol.iterator key (273 new) | ALLOW-list expansion: expand only members of a closed set of simple forms (identifier or string-literal key, plain/optional/readonly known, non-generic), decline everything else. Oracle generator iterates the GRAMMAR of member/key forms, not the findings. |
| C3 | Spelling used where binding is required | JSX usage by name, builtin `Array` by spelling, shadowed tags, AtFile scope, three path predicates for ambient/React | Resolve by binding or return unknown; one `declaration_origin`; no string equality on identifiers in decisions. |
| C4 | Derived state outside the dependency model | stale watch/lazy relevance (281), call-site cache, scheduler re-ask after edit (279/282) | Everything an answer reads is recorded (`deps`) or the answer is not kept; `watch_equals_fresh` model with mutation proof per dependency kind. |
| C5 | One decision, two owners | collapse lanes (267, 4 rounds), picked keys (4 readers), `annotate` x3, `{...props}` meaning, relevance map vs ADR | One function, one sink, provenance `(source, key, how)` not counts/names; lanes feed inputs, never decide. |
| C6 | Host assumptions | cgroup v1 mount (272) | Read the system's own description (mountinfo); fall back loudly. Fixed. |
| C7 | Hand-tuned policy without a reference model | scheduler fairness/starvation (279/281) | Property test against a reference model (sort by class, arrival) with the starvation rule as the spec. |
| C8 | Contract drift: code, ADR, schema disagree; fields defined but never populated | schema 8 per-component map vs ADR `used`, dead story-args, `used` empty on corpora, 281 | ADR is the contract; a field ships only with a producer, a consumer and a corpus count that is non-zero. |

Plus a process class: stacked PRs show the same code in every child (about 40% of the raw count) and merge commits
re-expose it. Remedy: merge in order, review once, retarget children.

## Pre-push gate (every slice, before the Entire reviewer ever sees it)

1. Invariants: write the 3 to 6 invariants of the slice in the PR body in these terms: 'unknown unless proven',
   'resolved by binding', 'every read recorded', 'one owner', 'wired or not defined'.
2. Grammar sweep: list every syntactic or type form the touched code can receive (all AST node kinds, all member
   and key forms, all declaration kinds) and show each one is handled or lands in the Unknown/Declined arm, by an
   EXHAUSTIVE match (no `_ =>`) or a generated test over the grammar with the oracle (checker, TS API) as judge.
3. Mutation proof: for each guard or dependency, remove it and show a test fails. A guard no test can fail is not a guard.
4. Adversarial pass: a reviewer that did not write the code gets the pattern list C1 to C8 and the grammar list and
   must try to produce a wrong output (not read the diff for style). Fix once, at the class level.
5. Then `/code-review medium` on the explicit SHA range, then push.
# Worker contract (caliper). Read once; the brief only names the task, the files you own and the call cap.

Scope
- Edit only the files the brief names. If another file must change, stop and say which and why.
- Never ask the user questions. If blocked, report what blocks and what you tried. Do not wait on background work: finish or report.

Branch and push
- Branch from origin/main unless the brief says otherwise. Own CARGO_TARGET_DIR under ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/<task>/. Scratch there too, never /tmp.
- Rust 1.99.1 on PATH (/Users/gabe/.rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin) for builds; commits need MISE_RUST_VERSION=1.99.1 (the mise shim forces 1.98.1). Caveat: with the toolchain bin first on PATH `rust-objcopy` can fail and strip silently does nothing; irrelevant unless you measure binary size.
- Signed commits ending `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`. Push normally (`git push origin HEAD:<branch>`), never --no-verify, verify the remote SHA with `git ls-remote`. Do not open or edit the PR, do not poll CI.

Checks: targeted, CI runs the rest
- Always, before push: `just lint doc-check machete typos` (fast).
- Then only what your change touches: Rust -> nextest of the touched crates; types/output/merge -> `just test-checker-lane` once; checker/session code -> gate_harness determinism and memory modes; output-preserving change -> full-content diff (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) of `extract --json --quiet --no-cache` vs a build of origin/main on ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large/src and ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/checker-default/chakra-only/src (tools: ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/perf-analysis/same.py, identity.sh; ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/final-perf/ab.sh interleaves two binaries).
- Do NOT run deny, semver, test-ts, test-napi, test-integration, test-py unless you changed those areas: CI runs them on every PR.
- Tests that fail on base for every behavior change. No oracle runs, no corpus fetches. No new scripts, options or recipes. Changeset only if `just semver` demands one.
- No wall-clock timing unless the brief asks; check `uptime`, and prefer allocation or instruction counts (load-independent).

Cap
- Stop and report after the call cap in the brief (default 60 tool calls) with what you have verified. Listing something as 'not done' with its cause beats burning more calls.

Artifacts (agents to agents; humans see them at the edge)
- Write the PR body to ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/pr/<branch, slashes as dashes>.md: `## What`, `## Evidence` (numbers, exit codes, what was diffed), `## Not verified`, last line `https://claude.ai/code/session_013R2ytvK9B32ZaSUaSe6aAZ`. The lead publishes it unedited.
- Final message <= 120 words: branch, head SHA (ls-remote verified), body path, blockers. Nothing else.

Pre-push gate (the reviewer must find nothing new; read ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/shrink/findings-synthesis.md, classes C1-C8)
- Guards are ALLOW-lists: handle a closed set of proven forms, everything else is Unknown/Declined (never 'complete', never 'none', never 'exact'). No `_ =>` arms in decisions over node/type kinds.
- Write the slice's invariants in the PR body (unknown unless proven; by binding not spelling; every read recorded; one owner; wired or not defined).

import * as React from 'react'

type BadgeProps = React.ComponentProps<'span'> & {
  /** Visual style. */
  variant?: 'default' | 'secondary' | 'destructive' | 'outline'
  asChild?: boolean
}

export function Badge({ variant = 'default', asChild = false, ...props }: BadgeProps) {
  return <span data-variant={variant} data-as-child={asChild} {...props} />
}
import * as React from 'react'
import type { ButtonProps } from '@chakra-ui/react'

type Size = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'
type Tone<T> = T extends 'danger' ? { confirm: boolean } : { hint?: string }

type Props<K extends 'danger' | 'calm' = 'calm'> = ButtonProps & React.ComponentProps<'button'> & {
  tone?: 'a' | 'b'
  fresh?: 'x' | 'y'
  size?: Size
  kind?: K
  extra?: Tone<K>
}

export function Button<K extends 'danger' | 'calm' = 'calm'>(props: Props<K>) {
  return <button {...(props as any)} />
}
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { Badge } from './Badge'
const meta = { title: 'Demo/A Badge', component: Badge } satisfies Meta<typeof Badge>
export default meta
export const Basic: StoryObj<typeof meta> = { args: { children: 'New', variant: 'secondary' } }
import type { Meta, StoryObj } from '@storybook/react-vite'
import { Button } from './Button'

const meta = { title: 'Demo/B Button', component: Button, tags: ['autodocs'] } satisfies Meta<typeof Button>
export default meta
export const Primary: StoryObj<typeof meta> = { args: { children: 'Hi', tone: 'a' } }
#!/bin/zsh
# usage: serve.sh <log> [cold]   starts the Storybook dev server on 6006; "cold" removes caliper-docgen's cache first.
cd $(dirname $0)
[ "$2" = cold ] && rm -rf node_modules/.cache/caliper-docgen
echo "start $(python3 -c 'import time;print(int(time.time()*1000))') load $(sysctl -n vm.loadavg)" > $1
exec npx storybook dev -p 6006 --ci >> $1 2>&1

"""Print rows (props + notableInherited) and layers of named components in an `extract --json` output.

usage: python3 rows.py OUT.json Name [Name...]
"""
import json
import sys

d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
comps = d.get("components", d)
items = comps.items() if isinstance(comps, dict) else enumerate(comps)
for _, v in items:
    n = v.get("displayName")
    if n not in sys.argv[2:]:
        continue
    props, notable = v["props"], v.get("notableInherited", {})
    print(n, "props", len(props), "notable", len(notable), "rows", len(props) + len(notable), v["filePath"][-50:])
    for layer in v["inheritance"]:
        print("  L", layer["typeName"], layer["fileName"][-45:], layer.get("htmlElement"), layer["totalProps"],
              "members", len(layer.get("members", [])), "used", layer.get("used"))
    parents = {}
    for p in list(props.values()) + list(notable.values()):
        key = (p.get("parent") or {}).get("name")
        parents[key] = parents.get(key, 0) + 1
    print("  parents", dict(sorted(parents.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:12]))
    if len(props) + len(notable) < 40:
        print("  names", sorted(props), sorted(notable))

"""Print rows (props + notableInherited) and layers of named components in an `extract --json` output.

usage: python3 rows.py OUT.json Name [Name...]
"""
import json
import sys

d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
comps = d.get("components", d)
items = comps.items() if isinstance(comps, dict) else enumerate(comps)
for _, v in items:
    n = v.get("displayName")
    if n not in sys.argv[2:]:
        continue
    props, notable = v["props"], v.get("notableInherited", {})
    print(n, "props", len(props), "notable", len(notable), "rows", len(props) + len(notable), v["filePath"][-50:])
    for layer in v["inheritance"]:
        print("  L", layer["typeName"], layer["fileName"][-45:], layer.get("htmlElement"), layer["totalProps"],
              "members", len(layer.get("members", [])), "used", layer.get("used"))
    parents = {}
    for p in list(props.values()) + list(notable.values()):
        key = (p.get("parent") or {}).get("name")
        parents[key] = parents.get(key, 0) + 1
    print("  parents", dict(sorted(parents.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:12]))
    if len(props) + len(notable) < 40:
        print("  names", sorted(props), sorted(notable))

Base directory for this skill: /Users/gabe/Projects/caliper/.claude/skills/adr

**Goal:** A future contributor (or you, in six months) understands why a hard-to-reverse architectural decision was made, in under a minute of reading.

## Decide if it's ADR material

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural** — it affects system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format/contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code** — if it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, skip it — it's a commit message, a code comment, or a line in `rdt-coverage.md`, not an ADR. A clever algorithm confined to one function, a naming convention, a behavior-preserving refactor: none of these are architectural even if someone spent real thought on them.

Unsure? Ask rather than guess — writing one nobody wanted is worse than skipping one that mattered.

## Write it

Full rules and voice guide: `docs/adr/README.md`. Template: `docs/adr/0000-template.md`. Read both before writing — don't rely on memory of them.

Find the next number by listing `docs/adr/*.md` and incrementing the highest. Copy the template, but treat its sections as a starting shape, not a form to fill mechanically — a one-paragraph decision doesn't need a forced "Alternatives considered" with nothing real in it. Cut sections that would just say "n/a."

Ground every claim in something checkable — a file, a line, a number, a test you actually ran. If you're about to write "this is faster" or "this was necessary," go verify it first (read the code, run the test, check git history) instead of asserting from a vague sense that it's probably true.

Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column. One line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap — matches every other doc in this repo.

## Before you save it

Read it back once as the target contributor, not the author. Cut every sentence that would survive being deleted — check against `docs/adr/README.md`'s banned-word list and before/after table. If a section reads like a corporate template ("In conclusion, this represents..."), delete it; ADRs stop when the decision's been explained, they don't wrap up with a summary of themselves.

Short beats complete. If the technical depth genuinely doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see how `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` points at `docs/type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.
